Production challenges

Improve onboardingProduction challenge · separate from shopper flow

Current source: five first-run screens; the user must choose at least one protected site. Top Sites suggestions are optional and unchecked. Travel/device sync is prechecked by default and stored as true unless turned off; that is an open consent decision, not proof of explicit opt-in.

Challenge: make the first-run journey clearer and production-grade while preserving explicit site choice, consent, a safe skip, and no automatic protection. Review the sync default before release.

Proof: source verified at manifest 1.4.103. No dedicated onboarding test was found in the current test set; browser/onboarding proof is incomplete.

Source scope: instructions.html, instructions.js, background.js; popup handoff in popup.html/popup.js.

Improve UIProduction challenge · use current popup

Design source of truth: the current popup, not the old design-document lime. Current popup tokens include lime #C8E88A, paper #F5F0E8, and surface #EBE4D4.

Challenge: improve hierarchy and usability without obscuring user choice, hiding important state, or introducing restriction language.

Proof: production-mode popup.js removes the QA panel, but background.js still lists copy-lab.js in protected-site injection. Production flags disable QA paths; they do not strip the code. tests/extension-mode.test.js checks flags, not the export allow-list. Package/browser proof remains incomplete.

Source scope: popup.html, popup.js, popup.css, and cognoscene-mode.js.

Before · Beta 1.2 Historical

Historical source snapshot only; the shipped Beta 1.2 build was not independently verified.

Start / endAction / UIEligibility / decisionStored state

START · first use
↓
01OnboardingSix-screen historical preview · begins here
  1. Welcome.
  2. Static protected-site preview; sample only.
  3. Preview a 48-hour hold and 24-hour decision window.
  4. Preview sample savings; not evidence of an outcome.
  5. Preview Urgente as one use per month.
  6. Finish writes onboarding completion, then opens the popup.
↓
02Protected-site setupPopup list · archived code snapshot
  1. Popup reads the stored protected-site list.
  2. User adds or removes a site; the list is written to Chrome sync storage.
  3. Only a matching protected domain enters the checkout check.
↓
03Checkout interceptionArchived flow is checkout-led, not browsing-led
  1. Trigger: a checkout attempt on a protected site.
  2. Read: protected-site list and existing hold timestamp.
  3. If no active hold, write a hold start to sync storage and show the hold overlay.
  4. Decision: take the historical “Bypass Test” path, or go back and leave checkout.
  5. If not bypassed, checkout waits through the 48-hour hold.
↓
04Decision window48-hour hold → 24-hour choice window
  1. After 48 hours, show “Buy now” or “Drop it” during the 24-hour choice window.
  2. Buy now removes the site hold and allows checkout for that session.
  3. Drop it asks for confirmation, then attempts cart clearing; the archived tests expect logging only after confirmed removal.
  4. On expiry, no silent cart clear; the next checkout check starts a new hold.
↓
END · buy, drop, or return to hold

Historical source gap: onboarding says Urgente is monthly, while the clean archive code shows a typing-test bypass. Actual shipped Beta 1.2 runtime is unknown.

Plain-text fallback
First run: welcome → static protected-site preview → 48-hour hold preview → sample-savings preview → monthly Urgente preview → finish / open popup.
Shop: popup site list → protected shop → checkout attempt → read site + hold state → historical hold / bypass-test path → 48-hour hold → 24-hour Buy now or Drop it → expiry prompt; no automatic cart clearing.

01Onboarding · production challengeExplicit setup is present; a production-grade redesign is plannedENHANCED

Verified currentPlanned challengeCurrent source has five screens; improving onboarding and UI remains Daniella’s challenge.

  1. Trigger Chrome opens the wizard on first install; an incomplete setup can reopen it after an update/startup.
  2. Eligibility / state read Read onboarding status, current settings, and any existing protected-site list before showing setup.
  3. UI Show five screens: welcome, site selection, checkout pause, evidence-first progress, and ready/privacy.
  4. User action The user adds at least one site to finish; optional Top Sites suggestions require a separate unchecked choice and explicit approval per site.
  5. State / event write Finish saves selected sites and onboarding/settings flags; skip saves completion/skip flags and settings without replacing the protected-site list.
  6. Next state Try to open the extension popup; if that fails, show the “open toolbar” fallback.
  7. Cooldown / reset / fallback No Top Sites access means no suggestions. Device-sync consent is currently prechecked and needs review in this challenge.
↓
02Protected-site shoppingOnly user-chosen domains are eligibleENHANCED

Verified currentTop Sites suggestions are separate from the explicit protection list.

  1. Trigger The user opens setup or chooses add/remove in the extension popup.
  2. Eligibility / state read Read protected domains and the separate Top Sites suggestion preference.
  3. UI Show the protected-site list; suggestions are visibly separate from protected sites.
  4. User action The user explicitly adds/removes a domain or accepts a suggested domain; nothing is auto-protected.
  5. State / event write Persist the protected-domain list in Chrome sync storage; Top Sites preference remains separate.
  6. Next state Only a listed domain becomes eligible for Observer, Product Pulse, and checkout checks.
  7. Cooldown / reset / fallback If suggestions are unavailable, show none; removing a domain removes its eligibility.
↓
03Observer + Product PulsePaired browsing and cart-growth branchNEW

Verified currentFive-return UI incompleteSource and focused tests exist; tests were not run for this handover.

  1. Trigger A protected shopping page receives qualifying browsing activity or a possible cart addition.
  2. Eligibility / state read Observer checks active-hold state, settings/cooldowns, at least one active minute, fresh scrolling and a natural pause. Product Pulse separately confirms a rendered cart increase.
  3. UI Show one eligible Observer check-in, or Product Pulse at seven confirmed items when its 60-second cooldown has elapsed; Rationalisation surfaces take priority.
  4. User action The user may answer, dismiss, or continue browsing; a reason is stored only when the user supplies it.
  5. State / event write Record bounded prompt/answer and confirmed cart-growth events; do not store product titles or infer intent.
  6. Next state After Product Pulse closes, defer Observer for five seconds, then resume only if it is still eligible.
  7. Cooldown / reset / fallback Enforce Pulse cooldown; uncertain DOM/cart evidence stays quiet. The fifth-return reason prompt is still missing in current source.
↓
04Rationalisation · checkout holdFirst qualifying checkout starts a 24-hour holdENHANCED

Verified currentMerchant proof incompleteStatic tests cover selected controls; browser support is not universal proof.

  1. Trigger A user activates a qualifying merchant checkout control on a protected brand; Cognoscene prompt buttons do not qualify.
  2. Eligibility / state read Read the brand hold, Urgente pass, and control classification. Unknown classification fails open.
  3. UI For an eligible checkout, show the 24-hour Rationalisation hold; normal browsing and add-to-cart remain available.
  4. User action The user can keep browsing, leave the merchant, or choose an optional in-hold route; no cart item is removed.
  5. State / event write Save the brand-scoped hold start and journey identifier in Chrome sync storage.
  6. Next state Preserve the original timer across reloads/brand subdomains; after 24 hours, open the separate 24-hour Deliberation window.
  7. Cooldown / reset / fallback Rationator does not restart the hold. After the decision window expires, a later checkout can begin a fresh hold; uncertain checkout controls fail open.

During the active hold · two optional routes, neither changes the timer

↶Rationator · return loopOptional pause while browsing during the holdNEW

Verified current sourceBrowser proof incompleteLocal per-tab/per-hold state only.

  1. Trigger During an active hold, the user selects “take a pause” from the hold reminder or uses its return action.
  2. Eligibility / state read Confirm the same hold is active and read its start plus per-tab/per-hold return state.
  3. UI Show optional hobby/work directions, careful browsing, back, and dismiss choices.
  4. User action The user chooses a direction, carefully browses, returns, or dismisses; Rationator does not decide or alter checkout.
  5. State / event write A careful-browsing choice records a site-and-hold key in tab session storage.
  6. Next state Return to the persistent Rationator card or reopen Rationator; the original hold and timer stay active.
  7. Cooldown / reset / fallback Clear the loop when the hold expires, is bypassed, or enters Deliberation; otherwise dismiss back to the active hold.
↗Urgente · unlimited useTyped, brand-specific, checkout-only passENHANCED

Founder-confirmedVerified currentLegacy monthly counter remains

  1. Trigger From the active checkout hold, the user chooses unlimited-use Urgente.
  2. Eligibility / state read Read the pass for that same brand; there is no monthly usage gate.
  3. UI Show the optional typing challenge.
  4. User action The user completes the phrase or cancels; cancel keeps the hold.
  5. State / event write On success, save a 12-hour same-brand checkout-only pass locally. Legacy monthly display/reset usage may increment, but never limits use.
  6. Next state Allow checkout only for the passed brand; Observer and Product Pulse remain separate.
  7. Cooldown / reset / fallback At 12 hours the pass expires; the next protected checkout reads the hold again. Repeated Urgente use remains unlimited.

Rationator loops back into the active hold. It is not a stage after the hold.

↓
05Deliberation · user choosesOpens after the 24-hour holdENHANCED

Verified current sourceNormal pass duration needs founder sign-offGrowth remains tentative and outside the active journey.

  1. Trigger The original 24-hour Rationalisation hold reaches expiry.
  2. Eligibility / state read Read the original brand hold, decision-window end, settled cart evidence, and pending user choice; uncertain cart facts remain unknown.
  3. UI Show the separate 24-hour decision window with continue/buy, wait, and selected-item edit options; never purchase automatically.
  4. User action The user explicitly continues/buys, waits, or edits their own merchant cart.
  5. State / event write Record the explicit choice; only confirmed cart changes may support a reduction record. Normal checkout-pass duration still needs founder sign-off.
  6. Next state An explicit buy/continue choice may grant temporary brand-scoped checkout permission; the merchant owns the cart.
  7. Cooldown / reset / fallback At expiry, remove the episode and show the brief “cart unchanged” notice with Continue browsing; a later qualifying checkout starts a fresh hold. Never claim savings, regret reduction, prevented purchases, or behavioural efficacy.

REMOVEDBeta 1.2 changes not carried into v1.3

The sample-savings preview and 48-hour hold are not carried forward. The old monthly Urgente cap is not a v1.3 rule; its historical runtime remains unverified.

Plain-text fallback
First run → improved onboarding challenge → user-selected protected sites → protected-site browsing: Observer + Product Pulse.
Merchant checkout action → 24-hour Rationalisation hold. During the hold: Rationator loops back into that same hold; Urgente is an unlimited-use, 12-hour, brand-scoped checkout-only branch.
After 24 hours → 24-hour Deliberation window → explicit user choice. Growth remains tentative and outside the active v1.3 path.
Shared ownership boundaries · click to reveal
  • Observer: owns optional browsing check-ins. Product Pulse is the confirmed-cart-growth branch within Observer, not a separate layer.
  • Rationalisation: owns the 24-hour hold. Rationator is an in-hold return loop; Deliberation is the separate post-hold choice; Urgente is the user-triggered, unlimited-use checkout pass.
  • Growth: tentative and grey. Cogno retains the scope decision; no Daniella runtime work or download until explicitly unlocked.
  • Python: shadow-only analysis; it has no live UI, eligibility, blocking, or decision authority.
  • Vision: planned fallback only after the DOM signal fails, never a parallel observer. Its current runtime wiring is unknown and needs an explicit contract before implementation.
